summary: Joseph E. Schwartzberg worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, Sorbonne, and University of Wisconsin–Madison under Richard Hartshorne, later serving as professor at the University of Minnesota from 1964 to 2000.

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at University College School and the University of London, he served as President of Harris Manchester College, Oxford, and held a post at Oxford (1889–1915).

Joseph Hackin worked in archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated in Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, he served at the Musée Guimet (1913–1941), École du Louvre, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and DAFA.

Joseph Haroutunian worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studies at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University, and Union Theological Seminary, he held posts at Wellesley College, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College and Harvard University under Robert A. F. Thurman, founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science, and was a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).

Joseph M. Kitagawa worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After degrees at Rikkyo, CDSP, Seabury-Western, and Chicago under Joachim Wach, he served as professor and Dean of the Divinity School at the University of Chicago (1951–1987).
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who completed his M.A. at Columbia University (~1948–1950) and held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University (1991).
Joseph Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017) under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and Collett Cox.

Joseph Needham worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. Educated at Oundle School and the University of Cambridge, he held posts at Cambridge (1924–1966), served as Master of Gonville and Caius College, and directed the Needham Research Institute (1976–1990).

Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy and religious studies. A former student of Bernard Williams, he served at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and held visiting professorships at United Theological College, UCSB, and the Ecumenical Institute of Bossey.

Joseph Ratzinger was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Munich and Ducal Georgianum, he held academic posts at the universities of Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen, and Regensburg between 1958 and 1977.

Joseph Rock worked in Sinology and Tibetology. He taught at Mid-Pacific Institute and served as a botanist and curator at the University of Hawaiʻi (1908–1920), an agricultural explorer for the USDA (1920–1924), and at the Army Map Service (1944).

Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held the post of Rector at St. Peter's College, Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Silvestre de Sacy, he served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, became Professor of Arabic at École des langues orientales, and presided over Société Asiatique.

Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held faculty posts at the École Normale Supérieure (1901–1907), the University of Paris (1907–1946), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1907–1950).
Joseph Walser is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (1788–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and held a professorship at Koyasan University (attested 1950).
Joshua Cutler works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ngawang Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).
Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Indology and Sinology. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (1794–1799), studied Chinese under Johannes Lassar, and founded Serampore College in 1818.
